Classic and new assets, at the pixels the game uses

The new VBXE v2 profile redraws the town, map, all fifteen building tiers, four arenas, three obstacles and all twenty-one six-pose fighter sets. Original assets remain intact. Use the same frame and zoom to compare.

All asset previews are decoded from the built 256-entry palette and VRAM data, including the actual packed local-palette animation frames. Game screens come from the assembled 6502 program running in the functional VBXE emulator. CSS only enlarges pixels; no smoothing is applied. This checks rendering and memory layout, not physical Atari timing.

What changed, and how to rebuild

Town and map preserve the five building plots, gate and five landmark identities. Building upgrades use clear roof-color families and a shared ground baseline. Native sprite extraction removes stray neighboring atlas pixels and reduces color noise; each new animation row shares no more than fifteen opaque colors plus transparency. Fighters remain 32×28, buildings 56×64, town/map 320×200, arenas 320×128. All four walk poses and two attack poses remain available. The new native building renderer preserves the original anchors while storing only opaque bounding rectangles, freeing VRAM for the fuller fighter art and extra idle caches.

Run python3 art/tools/prepare-vbxe-v2.py to extract the generated atlas sources. Run node art/tools/build-profile.cjs classic or node art/tools/build-profile.cjs vbxe-v2 to build in separate ignored working directories. The default native build continues to use classic art. Source assets and exact prompts are saved under art/vbxe-v2/; runtime replacements are in atari/city/assets/profiles/vbxe-v2/.

Use the wipe on scenery to inspect plot/hotspot placement, then compare all three building tiers in the real town screen. For fighters, use 6× or 8×, play Walk and Attack, pause and step frames. Artwork quality is a visual choice; both profiles are kept so individual assets can be revised or rejected.
